records.title: Aoife Wafer | RugbyPass Top 50 | #5
records.description: Still only 23, Wafer’s growing list of accolades is mind-boggling. In her first PWR campaign since joining Harlequins, the Ireland back-row scored seven tries and was named the club’s players’ player of the year while also earning a team of the season nod. Quins duly named her club captain ahead of her second year in the English top flight. At international level, Wafer’s calendar year ended quietly due to injury - she only featured against the USA in WXV and missed out against Japan and South Africa. Earlier in the year though, Wafer’s form was sufficiently strong for Ireland for the No.8 to again be crowned Women's Six Nations Player of the Championship and become the first woman to win the award in consecutive campaigns.

records.title: Meg Jones | RugbyPass Top 50 | #1
records.description: The Wales-born England centre has been a vital cog in the Red Roses machine over their last few years of dominance, particularly during their Women's Rugby World Cup win last year. Her performance against France in the semi-final inspired the Red Roses to get over the line and her try-scoring, tackle-thumping performances have made her a firm fan favourite. Her influence in the England side has only elevated further since she was given the captaincy at the start of this year and she has more than stepped up to the plate. It is clear her team-mates would follow her anywhere and her speeches post-match, shared on social media, show exactly why. The 30-year-old is not only an inspirational presence on the pitch but off it too, being incredibly open about grief, fertility and mental health.

records.title: Sylvia Brunt | RugbyPass Top 50 | #8
records.description: The dynamic inside centre from Auckland dominated senior club rugby aged 16 and was selected for Rugby World Cup 2021 [played in 2022] two years later as the youngest member of the winning squad at 18. Since 2023, she has played 31 of 33 possible Tests. Highlights include her 83rd-minute try to secure a 27-27 draw against Canada in 2025 and her player-of-the-match display in the 40-0 demolition of Ireland at Women's Rugby World Cup 2025 in Brighton. In 2026, she featured in nine Tests, scoring a try in the 48-15 win against the USA. Is there any woman who breaks more tackles than Brunt? At 22, she is already among New Zealand’s most capped midfield backs of all time with 40 and was named in World Rugby Women's 15s Dream Team of the Year 2026.

records.title: Pauline Bourdon Sansus | RugbyPass Top 50 | #4
records.description: Legend, leader, trailblazer and one of the greatest players to have ever graced the Test scene. The France scrum-half has the power, precision and knack of entangling even the tightest opposition defence, carving out a path for the Les Bleues even when there appears to be no space available. Bourdon Sansus has an extraordinary vision of the game, sensing opportunities where others see none and complementing that awareness with a level of passing few can rival. The 30-year-old was one of France’s standout performers at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 and 2026 Women’s Six Nations, and that’s unlikely to change in the foreseeable future.

records.title: Sadia Kabeya | RugbyPass Top 50 | #10
records.description: Sadia Kabeya is a player that does plenty of unseen work but provides exactly what England need in crunch moments. She is a tackle machine and integral to the Red Roses defence, which is exactly why she was player of the final in Women's Rugby World Cup 2025. It takes a special player to take Marlie Packer's number seven shirt, especially with Packer's form still impeccable, but Kabeya more than deserves her place. Her ability to read the game is second to none and aged just 24, she has an abundance of experience with 37 caps. The Loughborough flanker has already competed in two Women's Rugby World Cups and is surely one of the first names that will come to the mind of British and Irish Lions head coach Jo Yapp for the inaugural women's tour to New Zealand next year. Considering how good Kabeya is already, it is a scary prospect for opponents what she will become in the years to come.

records.title: Braxton Sorenson-McGee | RugbyPass Top 50 | #7
records.description: The 2025 World Rugby Women's 15s Breakthrough Player of the Year was a force of nature on attack at Women's Rugby World Cup 2025, leading in tries (11), points (69), metres gained (550) and clean breaks (15). The momentum continued in 2026. A stint with the Black Ferns Sevens saw Sorensen-McGee win an HSBC SVNS Series title, helping the Black Ferns Sevens to 30 wins in a row. In XVs, she helped the Blues win their third consecutive Super Rugby Aupiki title. She rejoined the Black Ferns in August and scored tries in the wins against Australia (66-19), South Africa (52-20) and France (31-12). In WXV Global Series, the 20-year-old full-back landed 13 goals from 16 attempts, slotting in seamlessly as a replacement for previous kicker Renee Holmes, and was named in the Women's 15s Dream Team of the Year 2026.

records.title: Ellie Kildunne | RugbyPass Top 50 | #6
records.description: Kildunne is the face of this all-conquering Red Roses team and that is down to her game-changing moments. The full-back's two tries against France in the Women's Rugby World Cup semi-final last year were moments of sheer brilliance that put England out of reach of Le Bleues. Her score in the final was breathtaking. England needed momentum back and Kildunne provided it, evading multiple defenders to run half the pitch to score. Her dazzling running, leaving Canadian defenders on the floor watching her, is one of the iconic images of that day. Her performances saw her finish runner-up in the BBC's Sports Personality of the Year award and helped to grow the popularity of the sport. Alongside Meg Jones and Jess Breach, she has also made the cowboy hat synonymous with this England team with their rodeo try celebration.

records.title: Kaipo Olsen-Baker | RugbyPass Top 50 | #9
records.description: The Black Ferns Player of the Year in 2024 has an enormous appetite for work and is arguably the most damaging ball-carrying loose forward in women's rugby. Just ask Canada. In the Pacific Four Series in April, Olsen-Baker scored two tries and charged over 200 metres in a brutal 36-14 revenge win after their 2025 Rugby World Cup semi-final defeat. In Super Rugby Aupiki 2026, Olsen-Baker scored a try in all six round-robin games and made more tackles (136) and carries (108) than any player in the competition. She has won 17 of her 23 Tests and has just been crowned World Rugby Women's 15s Player of the Year 2026 after an exceptional season.

records.title: Sophie de Goede | RugbyPass Top 50 | #2
records.description: Canada’s answer to legendary Australia World Cup-winning captain John Eales in the men’s game, a lock forward who can also kick goals, De Goede has become one of international rugby’s most respected players, with a skill-set which equips her to seemingly play in every position. A multiple PWR-title winner with Saracens - most recently being involved in their 2026 title - De Goede’s versatility to play in the second row and at loose forward is combined with her skill from the kicking tee, becoming Canada’s all-time leading points-scorer. The Canadian forward delivered on the international stage at the 2025 Rugby World Cup, finishing as the third-highest points scorer with 61, and helping Canada make it to the final. Crowned the 2025 World Rugby Player of the Year, she has just been named in the Women's 15s Dream Team for a third straight year, and fourth in all.

records.title: Zoe Harrison | RugbyPass Top 50 | #3
records.description: Harrison has been in and around the starting fly-half jersey for the Red Roses since her first cap back in 2017 but over the last two years in particular, she has made it her own. She manages the players around her superbly well and her goalkicking has been a real standout. During the 2026 Women's Six Nations, the Saracens star only missed two of 31 shots at goal, which made her England's most successful kicker across the women's and men's competitions. She is not immune to the pressure of course, missing a late penalty against New Zealand in September with the scores level, only to then pull off a superb intercept to score the winning try in the 81st minute and seal victory. The 28-year-old is only growing as a player with each game and is essential to England's continued success.

The All Blacks are winning, but could they still miss the Nations Championship final?

Plus, Ireland's resurgence, France's chances against the Springboks, and the crucial matches that could decide who makes the final.

You've never seen rugby like this before.

On 14 October 2023, Ireland and New Zealand's All Blacks played out one of the greatest matches of all time. Following over 100 years of dominance from New Zealand, Ireland had ignited the rivalry in recent years and headed into the 2023 World Cup quarter-final showdown as favourites on the back of three successive wins against the Men In Black. What unfolded was a fast, thrilling, heart-in-your-mouth spectacle that has to be seen to be believed.

records.title: Tests of Time: France vs South Africa - Is this the GREATEST game ever played?
records.description:
This is rugby like never before.
 
It was 15 October 2023 when Rugby World Cup hosts France and reigning champions South Africa went to battle in one of the most ferocious matches played in history, in front of a braying French crowd, hungry for blood and fire. With the poster boy of the rugby world Antoine Dupont at the helm, France entered their home tournament with high hopes of upsetting the apple cart and securing a first World Cup title for a Northern Hemisphere side since 2003. The indomitable Springboks, however, had mastermind Rassie Erasmus playing puppet master in the shadows - what had he cooked up for Les Bleus? Tune in for the cinematic clash between two rugby superpowers that delivered all the drama and all the physicality you could ever hope to witness.

records.title: Tests of Time: England v Australia - The night the rugby world stood still
records.description:
It's rugby - but not as you know it. Following a disastrous loss to Wales during the pool stages of the 2015 Rugby World Cup, England found themselves preparing for a do-or-die clash with Australia to avoid becoming the first-ever side to be knocked out of a home tournament. With Michael Cheika only recently taking over as head coach of Australia's Wallabies following a period of inner turmoil, it would take an unprecedented performance to etch their names into the history books. Who could have predicted what would unfold at Twickenham? Featuring Rupert Cox, Sean Maloney, Ben Coles and Neil Squires.
